result.title: Adaptive Action Horizon Selection via Flow-Field Uncertainty
result.summary: Reliable uncertainty estimates are important for adaptive execution in vision-language-action (VLA) models. Existing approaches such as Adaptive Action Chunking (AAC) estimate action entropy from multiple sampled action chunks, introducing additional inference cost and capturing both uncertainty within an action trajectory and diversity across alternative strategies. We introduce Divergence-based Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Action Chunking (DUAC), a post-hoc method that extracts trajectory-conditioned predictive uncertainty from the vector field of a pretrained VLA. Building on a closed-form flow-posterior covariance formulation, DUAC derives action-level uncertainty scores from a single generated chunk using Jacobian-vector products, without retraining or multiple endpoint samples. DUAC strongly correlates with AAC, while capturing distinct information: AAC measures global dispersion across sampled chunks, whereas DUAC measures local uncertainty around the trajectory selected for execution. Consequently, DUAC is less sensitive to diversity among distinct but valid action strategies. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa, DUAC-based adaptive horizon selection performs favorably among the evaluated methods, combining strong task success with low uncertainty-estimation latency. These results establish the flow vector field as an efficient, trajectory-conditioned source of predictive uncertainty for robot decision making.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DUAC，一种事后方法：基于闭式流后验协方差，用 Jacobian-vector 乘积从预训练 VLA 流场的单个动作块中提取轨迹条件预测不确定性，据此自适应选择动作执行视野，并在多个机器人操作基准上比较成功率与不确定性估计延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其从模型内部向量场以单样本、低成本方式估计轨迹局部不确定性并驱动执行长度选择，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的不确定性度量与 STOP 决策提供可核查的方法线索，但需确认该协方差近似能否迁移到非动作的推理状态序列。
